title: Spicy Mushroom Lasagne
subtitle: with a porcini and shiitake ragu
description: A lasagne built on a rich ragu of dried porcini, shiitake and wild mushrooms with chilli, finished with pecorino, parmesan and cream.

steps.text: Heat the vegetable stock only until it starts to bubble gently, remove from the heat and add the dried mushrooms and dried chillies. Soak for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 230°C and line a large rimmed tray with baking paper. Roughly chop the shiitake and wild mushrooms (in batches in a food processor or by knife), toss with 3 tablespoons olive oil and 1 teaspoon salt, spread on the tray and roast on the top rack for 30 minutes until golden brown, stirring about 3 times. Reduce the oven to 200°C and set aside.

Strain the soaked mushrooms over a bowl, pressing them against the sieve to extract the liquid. Roughly chop the mushrooms and finely chop the chillies. Measure the stock, topping up with water if there is less than 340 ml.
Finely chop the onion, garlic and carrot. Heat 60 ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the vegetables for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.

Finely chop the tomatoes and add to the pan with the tomato paste, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and 1 3/4 teaspoons pepper, and cook for 7 minutes. Add the soaked mushrooms, chilli and roasted mushrooms and cook for 9 minutes without stirring so they can brown a little.

Add the stock and 3 1/3 cups (about 800 ml) water, bring to a gentle boil, lower to medium and cook for 25 minutes until the ragu is very thick. Stir in 100 ml of the cream, cook for 2 minutes and remove from the heat.

Mix the pecorino, parmesan, basil and parsley in a bowl. Spread 1/5 of the ragu in a 28 cm round (or 20 x 30 cm) greased dish, sprinkle with 1/5 of the cheese mixture and cover with lasagne sheets, breaking them to fit. Repeat to make 4 layers of pasta and 5 layers of ragu and cheese.

Drizzle over a spoonful of the remaining cream and oil, cover with foil and bake for 15 minutes. Remove the foil, raise the oven to 230°C and bake for 12 minutes, turning the dish after about 6 minutes. Switch to the top grill for 2 more minutes until the edges are browned and crisp.
Rest for 5 minutes, drizzle over the remaining cream and oil, scatter with parsley and black pepper and serve.
